skill.name: deloreis
skill.description: Keep fiction and worldbuilding consistent with De Lore Is. Use when maintaining lore for AI-assisted novels, series bibles, campaigns, competing story ideas, retcons, or checks on generated additions to a fictional world. Record and query persistent lore through local MCP tools. Also use for explicit De Lore Is, DLI, or deloreis project requests.
skill.summary: Maintain structured fictional lore, check continuity, and track author-approved revisions through local De Lore Is tools.
skill.author: jeffreykentjr

content.user_title: Keep Fictional Lore Consistent with De Lore Is
content.value_statement: Fiction projects accumulate conflicting facts, unresolved alternatives, and revisions that are difficult to track. This skill guides local De Lore Is workflows for structured lore, continuity checks, and author-approved rulings.
actual_capabilities: Guide local runtime setup and project-scoped MCP registration using the included first-session walkthrough.
Record entities, facts, relationships, events, and event-anchored states through typed authoring tools.
Check structured claims against declared rules and explain findings through supporting claims and decisions.
Keep proposed alternatives and hypothetical accounts distinct from established lore.
Guide author-approved retcons while retaining earlier claim identifiers and decision history.
Guide rendered lore export and linked Markdown wiki generation using specialist tools and the CLI.
limitations: The skill does not install or bundle the De Lore Is runtime; a separate installation and client configuration are required.
Checks cover structured claims and recorded rules, not manuscript prose or every possible continuity error.
The host application must enforce approval, access control, and concurrent-write policy; some operations update the store directly.
World facts do not establish character knowledge, and De Lore Is is not general-purpose agent memory.

use_cases.title: Maintain a Novel Series Bible
use_cases.description: Query established character and setting facts before drafting, then check proposed additions against recorded lore.

use_cases.title: Track Campaign History
use_cases.description: Record campaign events, ordering, and changing allegiances without confusing story changes with retcons.

use_cases.title: Review Competing Story Accounts
use_cases.description: Compare proposed alternatives, inspect their consequences, and record the selected ruling while preserving earlier support.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Small Lore Project
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me set up De Lore Is for a small sample of my notes. Confirm runtime availability and ask which details are established.

prompt_templates.title: Check a Chapter Addition
prompt_templates.prompt: Query established lore relevant to this scene: [scene]. Propose its new factual claims, check continuity, and show conflicts before accepting changes.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Story Alternatives
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare these accounts: [alternatives]. Keep them proposed or hypothetical, explain their consequences, and ask for my ruling before changing established lore.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Traceable Retcon
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this revision: [revision]. Inspect support and differences, retain old claim IDs, and request approval before recording decisions or defeating earlier support.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: revising established lore with provenance

output_examples.input: In the first-session example, make Ashby Wren's home while the settled Thornfield home claim remains.
output: Continuity finding: Wren has two settled home claims, but home is declared single-valued.
The conflicting change cannot be materialized.
Choose whether to reject the addition, revise a ruling, or change the model.
Discarding staged claims does not undo decisions already recorded directly.

output_examples.input: Explain whether a clean De Lore Is check proves that my chapter is consistent.
output: A clean check covers the structured claims and recorded rules.
Review extracted claims against the chapter before accepting them.
Conflicts involving single-valued facts require the relevant predicate to be declared functional.

output_examples.input: Suggest a safe review process for two possible explanations of the same event.
output: Keep both explanations proposed or hypothetical.
Inspect established claims separately from possible accounts.
Compare findings and supporting decisions before choosing an account.
Record the author's ruling before making direct changes to accepted support.

best_practices: Start with a small sample, distinguish established facts from ideas, and agree on constraints with the author.
Inspect findings and differences before acceptance; follow host review policy before operations that update the store directly.
Track source decisions and claim IDs, refresh workspace digests after changes, and open a fresh workspace after another session commits.
anti_patterns: Do not change lore merely to silence findings or declare every predicate single-valued.
Do not treat chat recollection, edited wiki pages, or direct agent edits to rendered files as the project store.
Do not assume every mutation is staged or that discarding a workspace reverses recorded decisions.

faq.question: Does installing this skill install De Lore Is?
faq.answer: No. Install the runtime separately through Cargo or a release archive, then configure its local MCP server.

faq.question: Does the server require a hosted account or model API?
faq.answer: No hosted De Lore Is account or model API is required by the server. The writing assistant still uses its own model.

faq.question: Does De Lore Is check my entire manuscript?
faq.answer: No. It checks structured claims against recorded rules. Review extracted claims against the prose because unrecorded details are outside those checks.

faq.question: Can I keep alternatives without making them canon?
faq.answer: Yes. Keep alternatives proposed or hypothetical, and query the certain layer for established claims. Storing a note does not automatically establish canon.

faq.question: Does discarding staged work undo every change?
faq.answer: No. Decisions, defeats, and standing operations can update the store directly. Follow agreed rulings and host review policy before these calls.

faq.question: Can I export the lore as a wiki?
faq.answer: Yes. Export rendered lore with specialist tools, then use the static-wiki CLI profile. Editing generated wiki pages does not update the store.
